rows.definition: The OS page-cache reserve in fak's host-memory budget: an absolute byte floor held back from MemAvailable so demand-paged (mmap/pread) weights keep a read-through tier.
rows.distinction: Not the prompt-cache concepts (cache-read/cache-control), which meter provider token reuse; this is host RAM the kernel spends caching file-backed weight pages, and it is an ABSOLUTE floor rather than the fraction BudgetAfterHeadroom applies.

rows.definition: The demand-paged host fit guard: refuses a MemoryPlan whose host-scoped demands exceed HostBudgetForPagedWeights, the tighter of the fractional headroom budget and MemAvailable minus the absolute page-cache floor.
rows.distinction: Unlike RefuseHostScopedPlanIfTooBigForHost, which checks the fraction-only budget, this also carves out the page-cache floor, so it refuses a plan that fits the headroom term but would squeeze the read-through tier the mapped weights fault through.

rows.definition: The injectable core of RefusePagedHostPlanIfTooBig: takes the host (total, free, known) triple explicitly so the demand-paged refusal is testable without a live /proc/meminfo probe.
rows.distinction: Unexported test seam, not the entry point: RefusePagedHostPlanIfTooBig probes the live host via HostSystemMemoryInfo and delegates here, mirroring how refuseHostScopedPlanForHostMem backs the fraction-only guard in capacity.go.

rows.definition: The injectable core of RefuseHostScopedPlanIfTooBig (capacity.go): given a plan and an explicit host (total, free, known), it refuses when the plan's host-scoped demands exceed BudgetAfterHeadroom — the FRACTION-only host budget. Taking the host explicitly is what makes the refusal testable without a live /proc/meminfo.
rows.distinction: This is the FRACTION-only budget check; refusePagedHostPlanForHostMem is the demand-paged sibling that additionally subtracts an ABSOLUTE page-cache floor. They are not two spellings of one check: the fraction reserve scales with the box, while the paged floor is a property of the backing device's buffered-read cliff, so the two disagree on exactly the hosts where the choice matters. With floorBytes <= 0 the paged form reproduces this one byte-for-byte.
